question: Bind — ATK, full-buy, 3v5 down, 1:34 left. You are alone in B Long and the ult orb is right in front of you — 'HOLD F TO CAPTURE ORB (+1 ULT POINT)'. An Omen smoke covers the far end of B Long and an enemy is in that direction. Should you capture the orb?

options.label: Do NOT capture the orb — stay mobile, wide-swing the smoke line and take a clean duel first, then grab the orb if you're still alive
options.explication_courte: Capturing the orb is a 2-3 second channelled stationary action. In a 3v5 with an enemy in the smoke 10m ahead, you are defenceless the whole time — one sound cue and they swing and headshot you while you're locked in the capture animation. Win the duel first.

sources_option.citation: Stationary interactions (spike plant, orb capture, defuse) should only be committed when the immediate threat is neutralised; any enemy nearby makes the channel lethal

options.label: Capture the orb immediately — the ult point might be the difference-maker in a 3v5
options.explication_courte: Standing still for 2-3 seconds with an enemy at the end of the same lane is a near-certain death. An ult point you die getting is worth nothing. The 3v5 deficit cannot be solved by a power-up you never live to use.

sources_option.citation: Risk-reward principle: any channelled action with an immediate enemy present gives away your position and timing for free

options.label: Smoke off B Long exit with your signature, then capture the orb under the smoke cover
options.explication_courte: Using your signature to cover the lane before capturing is a real attempt to mitigate the risk, and it's defensible. The problem is the Omen smoke at the far end is already there — layering a second smoke means you're burning signature for an orb, a resource trade that's marginal in a 3v5 where you need every ability for the fight.

sources_option.citation: Utility spent to secure an orb rather than to facilitate a fight is a resource trade you must weigh against the ult value gained

options.label: Retreat out of B Long — the orb is not worth the exposure in a 3v5
options.explication_courte: Retreating cedes B Long entirely without gaining anything — no orb, no duel, no information. In a 3v5 every piece of map territory matters; giving B Long to the defense for free narrows your attack routes and gives them a free rotation lane.

sources_option.citation: Conceding space without a fight hands the defense free territory and rotation options; retreat only when the defensive cost of the lane is zero

explication_longue: The orb in B Long is a tempting target — an ult point that could matter in a 3v5 — but the tactical situation around it makes it a trap. Capturing any orb takes 2-3 seconds of standing stationary, and you have an enemy camped behind a smoke at the end of the same corridor. The moment you crouch to capture, you make the loudest 'free kill' sound available in the game: a locked-in channelling player with a known position. In a 3v5 your individual survival is critical to even having a chance at the round; dying for an ult charge you never use converts a tough 3v5 into an effectively unwinnable 2v5. The correct sequence is: engage the enemy in the smoke first, win the duel, and THEN collect the orb from safety if you're still standing. Using your own signature to create cover before capturing is a real compromise and not wrong — but it costs you an ability slot for an orb in a round where you need every tool for the actual site take. Simply retreating from B Long gives the defense the lane for free, no orb, no duel, nothing gained — the worst of all outcomes. Win the fight, then grab the reward.

sources.citation: Channelled stationary actions require a cleared immediate threat first; an enemy nearby turns any orb or plant into a defenceless death
